push_headlines: Friday's sell-off: the Dow -1.23% to 52,215.16 and the S&P 500 -0.52% to 7,623.68 as oil jumped.
Brent settled at $116.72 and WTI at $103.27, the highest settles since April, on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia.
Asia rebounded Friday: the Kospi +0.30%, the Hang Seng +0.69%, the Nikkei 225 -0.34%.
on_notice: Brent at $116.72 with a $120 bull case floated by analysts; watch the Sunday-night open for a gap in oil.
Reports of Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and a UAE oil spill keep Gulf supply in focus.
Energy was the lone bright spot Friday with the sector +2.50% to a record, while the Dow gave back 652.82 points.

asia.headline: Asia mostly rebounded Friday: the Kospi +0.30%, the Nikkei 225 -0.34%.
asia.detail: The Kospi closed at 5,550.30 after an early drop of about 2.4%, and the Nikkei 225 closed at 62,693.16 after recovering most of its losses. The Nikkei 225 is -4.03% on the week.

china.headline: Greater China higher Friday: the Hang Seng +0.69%.
china.detail: The Hang Seng closed at 23,093.37. The Shanghai Composite was +0.90% at 3,690.48 in the intraday report, and the official close was not confirmed.

mideast.headline: Brent settled at $116.72, the highest since April, on Gulf supply fears.
mideast.detail: Brent +3.14% at $116.72 and WTI +3.80% at $103.27 on Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and a reported UAE oil spill. Brent is about +6% on the week. On Wall Street the Dow -1.23% and the S&P 500 -0.52% as energy rallied.
